B"H

# Robots and Sitemap Architecture

Boruch Hashem. Blessed is He.

The Awtsmoos gathers every public doorway without confusing abundance with exposure;
Awtsmoos.com should show Google only canonical public vessels, while hidden chambers remain outside the map and the Torah road stays in repose.

## Evidence

- Geelooy has no root `_awtsmoos.derech.js`; root files are naturally static.
- There is currently no real `robots.txt` or sitemap implementation.
- `/api/social/heichelos/discover` already enforces persisted public visibility, `discoverable !== false`, and excludes debug, fixture, internal, staging, and test environments by default.
- Heichel discovery pagination uses `limit` plus an opaque `cursor`; `meta.pageInfo.nextCursor` and `hasMore` prove continuation.
- Series `details` includes both child `subSeries` IDs and posts.
- Numeric Road URLs canonicalize to named series-post URLs and therefore must not appear in sitemaps.
- Google supports multiple `Sitemap:` lines in robots.txt and recommends canonical absolute URLs in sitemaps.

## Chosen architecture

### Static root robots

`/robots.txt` is a static root file. It allows ordinary crawling and advertises:

- `https://awtsmoos.com/sitemap.xml`
- `https://awtsmoos.com/heichelos/sitemap.xml`

This avoids inventing a root dynamic router.

### Static root core sitemap

`/sitemap.xml` is a small root URL set for canonical public entry points only, initially `/` and `/heichelos`.

### Dynamic Heichel sitemap index

`/heichelos/sitemap.xml` is a sitemap index. It follows every page of the privacy-filtered public discovery API and emits one sitemap URL per discoverable Heichel:

`https://awtsmoos.com/heichelos/<encoded-heichel>/sitemap.xml`

### Dynamic per-Heichel sitemap

`/heichelos/:heichel/sitemap.xml` first proves the requested Heichel is present in public discovery, then traverses only that Heichel from series `root` through public series details.

It emits canonical URLs for:

- the Heichel root;
- every discovered named series;
- every stable named post under its containing series.

It never emits numeric Road positions, API routes, submit/edit/delete pages, or private Heichel identities.
